result.process_description:
This process begins with monitoring inventory levels in a warehouse or store.
When stock reaches a predefined threshold, an automated alert or manual check signals the need to reorder.
The procurement team then places an order with suppliers, considering factors like cost, delivery time, and supplier reliability.
Once the order is placed, the inventory system updates with expected delivery dates.
Upon receiving the stock, it is inspected for quality, recorded in the system, and placed on shelves or in storage.
The process ends when the inventory levels are updated after the restock is complete.

result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Use a parallel split when all outgoing branches start. Do not add decision conditions to parallel branches.
Use an inclusive split when one or more conditions can be true; use an inclusive join to synchronize only activated reachable branches.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Use gateways to control divergence and convergence, never to represent work. Identify exclusive, inclusive, parallel, event-driven or complex behavior.
Use an event-based gateway when the first occurring event selects the path. Target supported catching events or receive tasks, not ordinary tasks.

result.rule: When the description says an activity may or may not take place: Model the choice with an exclusive split: one path performs the optional activity and the other bypasses it. Rejoin the alternative paths with an exclusive merge when both continue into the same flow.

When the description presents mutually exclusive alternatives or says an activity may or may not occur, and the paths later continue in common: Model the choice with an exclusive gateway, and reconnect the alternative paths with an exclusive merge before their shared continuation.

When the description states a conditional outcome followed by intervening actions or an approval before a later activity: Model the branch through the described intervening actions and approval in the stated order; do not connect it directly to a later activity that bypasses them.

When the description identifies mutually exclusive destinations for an item or output: Model each destination as a distinct activity on an exclusive branch, then merge the branches before their shared continuation.

args.text: When the description states that multiple activities must all be completed before a shared continuation, model them as parallel branches and synchronize them before that continuation.
